The 'pre-approved' claims are not evidence, and no compliance review is recorded; the policy also states age verification is a legal requirement that cannot be relaxed by product choice.","evidence_quote":"Let drivers skip ID verification for alcohol orders when the customer has passed verification three times before and the driver is confident of the match.","citations":["policy-compliance#age-restricted-items"],"recommendation":"Obtain and record a Compliance review before proceeding; the legal requirement for age verification at handoff likely makes this proposal non-viable as written."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days is not the issue, but order-level randomization leaks across arms","detail":"Randomizing by order means the same customer and driver can be exposed to both skip and verify conditions, so arms leak. This is especially problematic since eligibility depends on a customer's prior verification history and driver judgment.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by order. Duration: 3 weeks.","citations":["experimentation-standards#pre-registration"],"recommendation":"Randomize at the customer or driver level (or by cluster) so exposure does not leak between arms, and document the unit and rationale."}]}
